## Visualizing the Trigonometric Functions and Their Unit Circle Projections

The following R code visually demonstrates the relationship between the three primary trigonometric functions—sine, cosine, and tangent—and their geometric interpretations on the **unit circle**.

- The **unit circle plot** shows how a point rotates around the origin for a given angle θ.  
- The **projections** of that point onto the x-axis and y-axis correspond to **cos(θ)** and **sin(θ)** respectively.  
- The **tangent** is represented as the slope of the radius vector, or equivalently, the vertical distance of the line tangent to the circle at \( (1,0) \).  
- The function plots show how each trigonometric function varies continuously with θ from 0 to 2π.

All plots are arranged together for a cohesive view of both the geometric and analytic representations of trigonometric functions.


```{r setup, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)

# Define theta (angles) and trigonometric values
theta <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = 400)
df <- data.frame(
  theta = theta,
  x = cos(theta),
  y = sin(theta),
  tan = tan(theta)
)

# Unit circle plot with projections
theta_highlight <- pi/4  # Example angle for projection (45 degrees)
highlight <- data.frame(
  theta = theta_highlight,
  x = cos(theta_highlight),
  y = sin(theta_highlight)
)

circle_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_path(color = "gray40", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "gray60") +
  geom_point(data = highlight, aes(x, y), color = "blue", size = 3) +
  geom_segment(data = highlight, aes(xend = x, yend = 0), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_segment(data = highlight, aes(xend = 0, yend = y), color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("Unit Circle and Trigonometric Projections") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

# Sine function plot
sin_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = theta, y = y)) +
  geom_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = theta_highlight, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(aes(x = theta_highlight, y = sin(theta_highlight)), color = "black", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Sine Function: y = sin(θ)", x = "θ (radians)", y = "sin(θ)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

# Cosine function plot
cos_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = theta, y = x)) +
  geom_line(color = "red", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = theta_highlight, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(aes(x = theta_highlight, y = cos(theta_highlight)), color = "red", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Cosine Function: y = cos(θ)", x = "θ (radians)", y = "cos(θ)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

# Tangent function plot (limited range to avoid infinities)
df_tan <- df %>% filter(abs(tan) < 5)
tan_plot <- ggplot(df_tan, aes(x = theta, y = tan)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = theta_highlight, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(aes(x = theta_highlight, y = tan(theta_highlight)), color = "blue", size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Tangent Function: y = tan(θ)", x = "θ (radians)", y = "tan(θ)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

# Combine plots using patchwork
(circle_plot | (sin_plot / cos_plot / tan_plot)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Trigonometric Functions and Their Unit Circle Connections",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"))
  )
```
